options: The risk that easily-copied digital currency could be spent more than once
The problem of Bitcoin transaction fees being too high
The difficulty of mining two blocks at once
A bug specific to the Ethereum blockchain
questions.explain: Since digital data can be copied like a file, every pre-Bitcoin digital currency had to solve how to prevent the same money from being spent twice.

questions.q: Why is Bit Gold considered a direct precursor to Bitcoin's architecture?
options: Its use of a growing chain of verified, timestamped solutions assigned to public keys closely resembles Bitcoin's own design
Bit Gold was literally the same software as Bitcoin
Bit Gold used no cryptography at all
Nick Szabo and Satoshi Nakamoto publicly worked together
questions.explain: Bit Gold's chain of solved puzzles tied to public keys already shows the shape of Bitcoin's chain and public-key ownership model, years before Bitcoin existed.

questions.q: Why did e-gold ultimately fail, despite real early popularity?
options: It wasn't decentralized — a single company controlled it, and the U.S. government was able to shut it down
Nobody ever used it
It was too expensive to operate
It was purely theoretical and never actually launched
questions.explain: e-gold's centralization was its fatal weakness — a single point of control the government could act against, unlike a genuinely decentralized system.

questions.q: What did the cypherpunk movement actually advocate for?
options: Widespread use of strong cryptography and privacy technology to protect individual rights and freedom
Banning all forms of encryption
Centralizing control of the internet under one authority
Eliminating all forms of digital currency
questions.explain: Cypherpunks pushed for tools like public key cryptography and VPNs to preserve anonymous communication, born out of concerns about government surveillance.

questions.q: Which real-world project is directly tied to the cypherpunk movement, according to this lesson?
options: PGP (Pretty Good Privacy)
Microsoft Windows
The original e-gold currency
The New York Stock Exchange
questions.explain: PGP, along with projects like the Electronic Frontier Foundation and the Tor Project, has direct roots in the cypherpunk movement's values.
